n: Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution
funding: The museum is a People's Liberation Army institution: Beijing's official tourism portal lists it as a deputy corps-level unit subordinate to the General Political Department, with the department's propaganda bureau as its professional supervisor. The Central Military Commission approved its name on 12 March 1959 and Mao Zedong wrote the inscription. Admission is free; the state rebuilt it between 2012 and 2017.
note: One of the Ten Great Buildings for the PRC's tenth anniversary, opened 1 August 1960 at 9 Fuxing Road; after the 2017 rebuild it has 159,000 square metres, 43 halls and over 160,000 relics.

propaganda.summary: The Central Military Commission approved the PLA museum in 1959; it opened in 1960 under the General Political Department. The Central Publicity Department named it a national patriotic education base in 1997; Xi led the Politburo Standing Committee there in 2017.

n: Memorial of the Site of the First National Congress of the CPC
funding: The Shanghai Municipal Committee of the Communist Party rented the site from 1951, bought it in 1952 and has shown it free of charge since 1952. The state built the new 3,700 square metre memorial hall across the street at 76 Xingye Road, opened by Shanghai Party secretary Li Qiang on 3 June 2021. The hall is led by a Party committee secretary and director, Xue Feng.
note: The 2021 exhibition holds 1,168 items; the hall counted 12 million visits between June 2021 and 2025, with 3.23 million in 2025, China Daily reports. Xi Jinping led the Politburo Standing Committee there in October 2017 to renew the Party oath.

propaganda.summary: The Shanghai Party committee bought the Party's birthplace in 1952 and opened it as a memorial. The Central Publicity Department named it a national patriotic education base in 1997; the state opened a tripled memorial hall for the 2021 centenary.

funding: A state museum founded on 1 July 1950, among the first revolutionary memorial halls of the People's Republic; the National Cultural Heritage Administration rated it a national first-class museum in 2008. Admission has been free since the enlarged building opened in August 2009. China Daily describes it as one of three national bases for patriotic education, revolutionary tradition and Yan'an spirit education.
note: The 29,853 square metre building at Wangjiaping holds over 38,000 relics and draws nearly 4 million visits a year; Xi Jinping took the new Politburo Standing Committee there on 27 October 2022.

propaganda.summary: The state founded the hall in 1950 to display the Party's thirteen Yan'an years. The Central Publicity Department listed the Yan'an memorial sites as national patriotic education bases in 1997; Xi led the Politburo Standing Committee there in 2022.

n: Memorial Hall of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
funding: A state memorial first built in 1958, moved to its present site in 1993, and closed in December 2014 after the central government approved its renovation and expansion in June 2014. It reopened on 19 September 2020 for the war's 70th anniversary with free admission. Xinhua describes it as a national patriotic education demonstration base; the museum's director is Liu Jingyuan.
note: The 182,000 square metre site at 7 Shanshang Street holds a 23,845 square metre exhibition hall, a 53 metre memorial tower, a panorama hall and a national defence education park; it recorded 12 million visits before the 2014 closure.

propaganda.summary: Built by the state in 1958 as China's only Korean War museum and listed as a national patriotic education base in 1997. The central government approved its expansion in 2014; it reopened in 2020, which historians told SCMP warns the US and rallies Party support.

n: Museo de la Revolución Democrática y Cultural
funding: The Bolivian state built the museum through the Fondo Nacional de Inversión Productiva y Social for almost 50 million bolivianos, opening it on 2 February 2017 in Evo Morales's birthplace. In June 2023 Culture Minister Sabina Orellana said the FPS and the Andamarca municipality still administer it because it was never legally transferred to the Ministry of Cultures, which pays only periodic security costs. The museum has been closed for over three years, Orellana said in December 2023.
note: Three blocks totalling about 3,855 square metres on a 12,000 square metre site, with an open-air theatre and Andean temple, in a village of about 163 people; the Viceministry of Tourism reported 17,000 visitors in its first year.

propaganda.summary: Evo Morales ordered the museum after his 2006 election; his government opened it in 2017 to show his life, the gifts he received and his achievements. Critics called it a personality cult; it closed after his 2019 fall.

funding: The Politburo of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party decided on 16 December 1992 to build the museum, which opened on 13 December 2000 for Kaysone Phomvihane's 80th birth anniversary. It was built with non-refundable aid from the Vietnamese government, and in March 2014 Vietnam approved a further 14 billion dong (658,000 dollars) refurbishment implemented by the Ho Chi Minh Museum. The Lao state operates it as a memorial and educational institution.
note: A bronze statue of Kaysone stands outside; the Party's Propaganda and Training Board stages its anniversary exhibitions here, opened by Party General Secretary Thongloun Sisoulith in 2025.

propaganda.summary: The Party Politburo decided in 1992 to build a museum to the Party's founder; Vietnam funded it and it opened in 2000. The Party's Propaganda and Training Board holds exhibitions there to educate the public in Party traditions.

funding: The Bangabandhu Memorial Trust, founded and chaired by Sheikh Hasina, owned and ran the museum in Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's house at Dhanmondi 32 from its opening on 14 August 1994; Hasina chaired trust meetings there as prime minister. Banks donated 1,360 million taka to the trust in 2017 and Standard Bank 100 million taka in 2020. The museum was burned on 5 August 2024 and demolished on 5 to 6 February 2025; the Yunus government then revoked the trust's tax exemption.
note: The house where Mujib was killed in 1975, with a six-storey extension added in 2011; on National Mourning Day the president, prime minister and armed forces held state ceremonies there until 2023.

propaganda.summary: Sheikh Hasina's trust opened the museum in her father's house in 1994. As prime minister she held state salutes and Awami League wreath ceremonies there each 15 August. Protesters calling it a shrine of fascism burned it in 2024 and razed it in 2025.

funding: A state museum created by Ordinance 66-72 of 2 December 1972, inaugurated on 5 July 1982 beneath the Maqam Echahid martyrs' monument at Riadh El Feth, and placed under the Ministry of Mujahideen in 1993, which supervises it today. Entry costs 20 dinars and is free for mujahideen and soldiers. The museum's stated mission is to preserve the memory of the Revolution and the struggle against French colonisation.
note: Underground beneath the 1982 monument's esplanade, with wings on the resistance from 1830, the 1954 to 1962 war and independence; the monument was built by the Canadian firm Lavalin to a design by Bachir Yelles.

propaganda.summary: President Chadli unveiled the Maqam Echahid complex in 1982 to represent national unity and strengthen the FLN regime's legitimacy, Sarah Gray writes in Ibraaz. The museum, built 1981 to 1984, has run under the Ministry of Mujahideen since 1993.

funding: The museum operates under the Central Military Commission, the Ministry of National Defence and the General Department of Political Affairs of the Vietnam People's Army, the army newspaper Quan Doi Nhan Dan reports. The state funded the new 2,500 billion dong (101 million dollar) building on Thang Long Boulevard as a special-grade army project managed by the General Political Department; it opened on 1 November 2024 with free admission to the end of that year.
note: A 64,640 square metre building on a 74 hectare site with a 45 metre Victory Tower, over 150,000 artefacts and four national treasures; Party General Secretary To Lam visited on 3 December 2024.

propaganda.summary: The army's General Political Department built the new museum, opened in 2024 to honour the People's Army and build pride in the defence tradition. Party chief To Lam called it a red address for studying the Party's leadership in every period.

funding: A branch of the state-run National Historical Museum of the Republic of Belarus, created by the Ministry of Culture and opened in 2012 for the 20th anniversary of Belarusian sovereignty, as the ministry's Svetlana Gavrilova announced. State bodies lent exhibits for its collection of over 4,000 items. It occupies the Presidential Administration building at 38 Karl Marx Street.
note: Six halls on Belarus from 1990 to the present, showing the first presidential decrees, state awards, gifts to Alexander Lukashenko and models of state buildings; Lukashenko called its opening of great political importance.

propaganda.summary: The Ministry of Culture opened the museum in 2012 inside the Presidential Administration to present the achievements of the presidential state since 1994, with Lukashenko's first decrees and gifts to him. Lukashenko called its opening of great political importance.
